 The Crew Chief, Aircraft Maintenance reports to the Maintenance Manager, as assigned. In the role of Crew Chief you will plan, develop, manage, oversee, and perform maintenance, repair, modification, inspection, and record keeping activities for RTFlight aircraft to assure the proper functioning, high availability and airworthiness of aircraft, equipment, and accessories consistent with the procedures and standards of RTFlight.
 What You Will Do 
 Manage and perform aircraft scheduled and unscheduled maintenance supporting RTFlight missions, including aircraft departure and arrival activities. 
 Plan, implement, and maintain effective procedures, policies and systems for the scheduling and maintenance of aircraft. Ensure accurate, current, and complete documentation is utilized and maintained to include records, inspection programs, and maintenance manuals. Ensure that RTFlight standards and effective cost controls are adhered to, and that aircraft maintenance operations are performed in accordance with requirements, schedules, and commitments.
 Oversee offsite major repair and overhaul projects and the conduct of all such services necessary to achieve compliance with RTFlight standards and FAA regulations.
 Perform on-site inspection, maintenance, repair, modification, and test of RTFlight aircraft and component equipment, including sophisticated electronic navigational and control devices, mechanical and hydraulic systems, and gas turbine engines.
 Crew Chiefs will be trained and capable on all RTFlight aircraft. They will also be focused on one airframe type for additional duties and training. Additional responsibilities include, inspection packages, due lists, logbook entries, audits, and research.
 Establish priorities and coordinate with appropriate RTFlight supporting departments or contractors to ensure aircraft is airworthy and the facility is properly maintained. This may include oversight of the passenger accommodations and hangar facility including janitorial services, and maintenance of associated ground support equipment. This also includes maintaining an adequate supply of tools, serviceable parts, components, and consumables necessary for servicing and maintenance of assigned aircraft.
 Manage aircraft maintenance costs in a manner which assures that both operating, and capital budgets are considered during decision making; and as necessary, provide support in the development of financial plans for aircraft maintenance and facilities operations.
 Prepare estimates on costs of labor and materials for future work to be performed on aircraft to include down-time needs; and provide scheduling input with Maintenance Managers for all work to be performed.
 Provide management of general facilities maintenance, housekeeping, and oversight of RTX Environmental Health and Safety policies and procedures specific to activities being conducted within RTFlight leased, rented, or owned properties.
 Order parts, components, tools, consumables, and supplies consistent with areas of responsibility and provide the validation, proper account assignments and pre-approval in the review of vendor billings or charges. Manage spares inventory for aircraft, including ordering, completion of required documentation and performing receiving inspections.
 Maintain and complete all processes within span of control in accordance with current RTFlight Quality Management System and ISBAO requirements/procedures.
 Ensure that all activities are in compliance with all appropriate Raytheon Technologies and Government guidelines.
 Perform additional tasks and acquire varying responsibilities as appropriate.
 Must be able to travel worldwide without restriction, up to 10% travel.
 Qualifications You Must Have 
 Typically requires a University Degree and minimum 5 years prior relevant experience or an Advanced Degree in a related field and minimum 3 years of experience or in absence of a degree, 9 years of relevant experience.
 Must hold a valid A&P Certificate .
 Demonstrated knowledge of the Flight Operations Manual; and demonstrates knowledge of the CFRs and standards relating to aircraft maintenance.
 Qualifications We Prefer 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 Additional aircraft training courses.
 What We Offer 
 Whether you’re just starting out on your career journey or are an experienced professional, we offer a robust total rewards package with compensation; healthcare, wellness, retirement and work/life benefits; career development and recognition programs. Some of the benefits we offer include parental (including paternal) leave, flexible work schedules, achievement awards, educational assistance and child/adult backup care.

You turn scrollers into followers… and followers into customers. You know how to make people stop, watch, follow, click… and buy. Likes are nice. Views are nice. But sales are nicer. Because great organic social doesn’t just build an audience. It earns attention, builds trust, and turns that trust into measurable revenue.
 If that sounds like you, you might have what it takes to become our next Organic Social Specialist. 
 Small Print ⇒ We’re not looking for a “like junkie.” We want someone who knows how to grow a social audience and turn that attention into sales. Someone who understands that followers, views, and engagement are only useful if they build trust, drive traffic, and ultimately help customers buy. If you measure success by views alone then this probably isn’t the role for you.
 Still here?
 Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels: 
 We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your work will help more women discover those solutions. You’ll help us become a brand these women actually want to follow. You’ll help create the posts that make her stop. The videos she sends to a friend. The content that makes her think, “Finally. Someone actually gets it.”
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than here.
 This job might be for you if… 
 You understand what makes people stop scrolling . Hooks. Thumbnails. First frames. Captions. Curiosity. Emotion. Pattern interrupts. Trends. You don’t need someone to explain why the first two seconds of a TikTok matter. You already spend more time than is probably healthy wondering why one piece of content gets 327 views while another gets 327,000.
 You know every platform speaks a slightly different language. TikTok isn’t Instagram. Instagram isn’t Facebook. YouTube isn’t Reddit. And taking the exact same post, resizing it four times, and calling it a “social strategy” makes a small part of you die inside. You know how to adapt an idea to the platform, audience, format, and reason somebody is there in the first place.
 You can actually create the stuff. We’re not looking for someone who just sits in meetings talking about content pillars. You’ll help develop ideas, write briefs, schedule content, coordinate assets, get everything live, and make sure the little details don’t fall through the cracks.
 You’ve got a nose for a good trend. Sounds. Formats. Memes. Conversations. Creators. Questions people suddenly can’t stop asking. You pay attention to what’s happening online and can tell the difference between a trend we should jump on… and one that will make a women’s health company look like someone’s dad discovered TikTok.
 You’re obsessed with the audience. What are women talking about? What are they frustrated by? What are they asking in the comments? What myths keep popping up? What are competitors saying? What language are real women actually using? You know some of the best content ideas won’t come from a brainstorm. They’ll come from listening.
 You care about results more than vanity metrics. Followers and likes are lovely. But you also want to know what people clicked, what sent traffic to the site, what converted, what content assisted a sale, and what we should do differently next month. Because ultimately, we’re not trying to win a trophy for “nicest Instagram grid.”
 Numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. Reach. Engagement. Clicks. Conversion. Follower growth. Traffic. UTMs. GA4. You don’t have to be a data scientist wearing six monitors and muttering about statistical significance. But you should be able to look at performance, spot patterns, and turn what you learn into better content.
 You know how to use social scheduling tools without needing an emergency tutorial. Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Later, Buffer, or something similar. We don’t care which logo you’ve stared at most. We care that you understand how to plan, schedule, organize, and manage a social calendar without everything descending into chaos.
 You can turn performance into strategy. You don’t just send a monthly report containing 17 charts and the groundbreaking observation that “engagement was up.” You ask why. What worked? What flopped? Which topics got attention? Which formats drove clicks? What should we do more of? Less of? Test next? The report is only useful if it changes what we do.
 You’re organised enough to keep a lot of little moving pieces moving. Content calendars. Briefs. Designers. Video. Approvals. Links. UTMs. Scheduling. Launch dates. Reporting. Somebody has to keep track of it all. Preferably without sending 14 Slack messages asking, “Any update on this?”
 You play nicely with others. You’ll work with Content, Creative, Acquisition, Email, Influencer, Customer Service and other teams across the business. Sometimes you’ll need something from them. Sometimes they’ll need something from you. You communicate clearly, follow up, solve problems, and understand that being easy to work with is a genuine career superpower.
 You know social never stops changing . Algorithm updates. New features. New formats. Social commerce. Search behaviour. Yesterday’s “best practice” suddenly dying a very public death. You’re curious enough to keep learning without somebody having to chase you around the office waving an industry newsletter.
 You’ve got at least a year of experience in social media marketing or something closely related. Maybe you’ve managed brand accounts. Maybe you’ve built social for an ecommerce company. Maybe you’ve helped grow a community, supported creator campaigns, or owned organic content as part of a broader marketing role. What matters most is that you can show us you’ve done the work and learned from it.
 Women’s health genuinely interests you. You don’t need to arrive knowing everything about women’s health. But you do need to care enough to learn. We’re talking about real health concerns affecting millions of women, so curiosity, empathy, accuracy, and good judgment matter.
 Bonus points if you’ve worked with Shopify, ecommerce brands, Google Sheets, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools.
 Double bonus points if you already have strong opinions about why most brand TikToks are painfully boring.
 Now, time to be honest… is this really you?
 If you’ve already started thinking about what you’d post first, which competitors you’d stalk, and how you’d build our first 10,000 followers…
 We should probably talk. 
 We don’t expect you to know everything. This isn’t a “12 years of TikTok experience required” job ad. But we do want somebody curious, switched on, commercially minded, organised, and hungry to get very, very good at organic social.
 And someone who sees a brand starting from scratch and thinks:
 Ohhh… this could be fun. 
 Other Qualities You’ll Need
 We’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble — you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own.
 You’re hungry — you want to learn more, improve, and keep getting better.
 You’re people-smart — in the sense that you’re a great teammate.
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at our company.
 So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that’s a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?
 We believe in rewarding top talent.
 So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills, curiosity, and hunger to grow, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 An incredible dog-friendly office
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave.
 Culture is everything to us.
 Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible.
 But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply
 So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of Team AlgaeCal?
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer the right person.
 So, to make sure our future Organic Social Specialist is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive here, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application.
 If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume and cover letter.
 Please read carefully: 
 1. Write a cover letter addressing:
 Why are you the best Organic Social Specialist for this role? Give us examples of accounts, campaigns, or content you’ve worked on — and include results where possible.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What’s the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?
 What are the last three books you’ve read?
 What do you do for fun?
 2. Explain what you’re doing now for a job:
 If you don’t have one, explain why.
 If you have one, explain why you’re looking elsewhere.
 3. Show us what you’ve done.
 Please include links to social accounts, campaigns, posts, videos, or other work you’ve helped create or manage.
 And tell us what you actually did. 
 If something performed particularly well, even better. Give us the numbers.
 4. Upload your cover letter and resume.
 Ensure your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 Yes, our hiring process is challenging, but it’s our way of selecting the best — and your way of ensuring your AlgaeCal teammates are tops.
 Click the “Apply Now” button on this page and upload your cover letter and resume. 
 Note: Please include your cover letter WITH your resume in one document. Applications without a cover letter will not be read! 
 We’re looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly and you can expect a prompt response.

 Aspire Software recherche un directeur ou une directrice de l’exploitation (COO) pour l’une de ses unités d’affaires spécialisées dans les logiciels !
 Ce poste joue un rôle essentiel dans la direction opérationnelle et commerciale d’une entreprise évoluant dans un secteur logiciel en croissance. Vous serez responsable de l’élaboration et de la mise en œuvre du plan stratégique de l’entreprise, couvrant les ventes et le marketing, le soutien à la clientèle et les services professionnels.
 La personne retenue devra définir et mettre en œuvre les stratégies nécessaires pour atteindre les objectifs de croissance et d’exploitation, en mettant l’accent sur l’excellence opérationnelle. Elle devra adopter une approche axée sur l’intelligence artificielle pour concrétiser nos plans de croissance.
 Quelques mots sur notre entreprise : Aspire Software, une division opérationnelle de Valsoft Corp, exploite et gère un portefeuille de sociétés de logiciels détenues à 100 %, qui proposent des solutions essentielles aux activités de leurs clients dans plusieurs secteurs. En appliquant les meilleures pratiques du secteur au sein d’un modèle décentralisé, Aspire stimule une croissance rapide en réinvestissant dans les entreprises de son portefeuille.
 Responsabilités générales 
 Élaborer et mettre en œuvre une stratégie d’IA pour les fonctions autres que la recherche et le développement. 
 Assumer la responsabilité des objectifs financiers et non financiers à long terme, annuels et trimestriels. 
 Définir et communiquer une vision claire des objectifs, des stratégies et des principes en matière de croissance, de génération de revenus, de rentabilité et de service à la clientèle. 
 Participer activement aux activités quotidiennes, notamment à la performance commerciale, à la gestion des occasions de vente, aux prévisions, à l’affectation des ressources aux services, au soutien à la clientèle et à la réalisation des projets clients. 
 Ventes et marketing 
 Stimuler la croissance du chiffre d’affaires en collaborant avec l’équipe commerciale pour repérer de nouvelles occasions et mettre en œuvre des stratégies de croissance, notamment les ventes croisées, les ventes additionnelles et l’expansion vers des marchés connexes. 
 Mettre en place des pratiques et une infrastructure de gestion des ventes de premier plan pour soutenir efficacement la croissance et assurer la rigueur des processus. 
 Élaborer et maintenir des programmes de veille concurrentielle et produire des rapports sur les tendances du secteur pour orienter le développement de nouvelles fonctionnalités et de nouveaux produits. 
 Optimiser l’utilisation du CRM et des autres outils internes pour améliorer les prévisions, mettre en place des objectifs et fournir des analyses exploitables à l’équipe de direction et au conseil d’administration. 
 Définir et mettre en place des indicateurs clés de performance pour mesurer l’efficacité et la productivité de l’équipe commerciale, notamment le coût d’acquisition client (CAC) et la valeur vie client (LTV). Créer des tableaux de bord et établir un processus de suivi des résultats, notamment des tendances de rétention nette des revenus (NRR) et de revenus mensuels récurrents (MRR). 
 Collaborer avec les responsables des ventes pour définir les quotas, les budgets et les plans de rémunération, et optimiser la tarification. 
 Assurer la gestion des relations stratégiques avec les grands comptes. 
 Participer à des salons professionnels et à des tables rondes. 
 Service à la clientèle et réussite client 
 Mettre en œuvre un programme de réussite client efficace et durable. 
 Déployer et maintenir des initiatives de soutien à la clientèle. 
 Animer des formations à l’interne et auprès des clients. 
 Suivre et documenter les indicateurs de réussite client, notamment l’utilisation du programme, les niveaux de satisfaction, le volume de demandes d’assistance traitées et leur résolution. 
 Coordonner les enquêtes annuelles de satisfaction client, notamment le Net Promoter Score (NPS), ainsi que les autres outils de communication. 
 Services professionnels 
 Assurer la rentabilité des projets en suivant le taux d’utilisation facturable des équipes, les charges d’exploitation liées au personnel et la marge contributive. 
 Définir des stratégies pour accroître la rétention nette des revenus (NRR). 
 Effectuer un suivi mensuel des résultats avec la personne responsable des services professionnels. 
 Votre profil 
 Baccalauréat ou diplôme équivalent, de préférence dans un domaine technique ou en administration des affaires, MBA ou diplôme d’études supérieures. 
 Au moins cinq ans d’expérience en gestion directe d’équipes multidisciplinaires et en gestion d’un compte de résultat dans le secteur des logiciels SaaS spécialisés par marché vertical, idéalement dans le tourisme et les loisirs. 
 Expérience dans l’amélioration de l’efficacité des ventes, du marketing, du soutien à la clientèle et des services professionnels grâce à l’automatisation par l’IA. 
 Une expérience en approvisionnement de matériel et en traitement intégré des paiements constitue un atout. 
 Aptitude naturelle à piloter la performance et à assurer la santé financière d’une entreprise. 
 Esprit entrepreneurial démontré et capacité à donner le rythme. 
 Solides compétences financières à l’échelle de l’organisation, notamment en compréhension des documents financiers, en intelligence d’affaires et en planification et analyse financières (FP&A). 
 Expérience avérée dans l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de stratégies efficaces d’acquisition de nouveaux clients et de pénétration de marchés. 
 Capacité à structurer, à analyser et à résoudre des problèmes d’affaires complexes, tout en produisant des résultats concrets par rapport aux objectifs de l’entreprise. 
 Excellentes compétences en leadership, en communication et en organisation. 
 Approche pratique et volonté de mettre la main à la pâte pour résoudre les problèmes.

Providing assurance on the effectiveness of post-trade compliance, the CCO reports directly to the Board of Directors and the Vice President, Regulatory Affairs and Enterprise Compliance.

 Serve as a strategic advisor on the compliance impact of changes to post-trade businesses, including changes to rules, risk frameworks and IT infrastructure

About KidKare 
 The people who care for and feed children every day have enough on their plates. Their software shouldn't add to it. 
 For more than 30 years, KidKare has built technology for the people behind childcare and child nutrition, helping them spend less time on paperwork, compliance, and administrative work and more time focused on the children and communities they serve.
 Our roots run deep in the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), a federal nutrition program that helps provide healthy meals and snacks to children and adults across the country. Today, we're building on that expertise with a growing ecosystem of software supporting childcare organizations across food program compliance, business management, professional development, and licensing.
 We're growing into new products, new markets, and have a much bigger vision for what KidKare can do for the childcare community. To support these goals, we're looking for a Product Growth Marketing Manager, Lifecycle & GTM Systems to build and run the engine that turns our product value into pipeline, adoption, and revenue.
 Position Summary 
 This is an execution-first growth role.
 You'll partner with Product and Revenue Operations leadership to define the positioning and value proposition for each product, then put them to work: translating individual product propositions and features into audience-specific messaging and deploying that messaging through various tactics. You’ll be involved in managing the CRM, data enrichment, prospect scoring, routing, & lifecycle marketing. You'll report to our VP of Revenue Operations and work across Product, Sales, and Customer Growth to turn every launch and feature release into measurable pipeline, adoption, and expansion.
 In a given week you might ship a new CRM workflow, tune a fit-and-intent scoring model, launch a demand-gen test to a newly enriched segment, build an app telemtry guide for a feature release, fix a routing rule that's sending leads to the wrong queue, or walk leadership through what moved in the funnel and why.
 You'll build the machine, and you'll run it. 
 You'll partner closely with our Digital Marketing Manager, who owns brand, creative, content, and channel execution. You'll own the systems, segmentation, lifecycle logic, experiment design, and measurement that make that work reach the right audience at the right moment. Together, you'll turn product and market insight into demand.
 Primary Responsibilities 
 Positioning, Feature Messaging & Launch Execution 
 •    Partner with product leadership to define and refine positioning and value propositions for each product and major release, grounded in customer, competitive, and market insight.
 •    Translate individual product features and releases into audience-specific messaging (the value, the proof, and the call to action) for each persona and segment we serve, carrying positioning down to the feature level.
 •    Execute launches through the systems you manage: target segments, lifecycle and nurture workflows, in-app guides, sales sequences and snippets, with launch tiers matched to the size of the release.
 •    Package features into the battlecards, talk tracks, and objection handling our Sales and Customer Growth teams need, delivered inside CRM where reps actually work.
 CRM Management & GTM Systems 
 •    Manage the CRM as the system of record for marketing and lifecycle: data model, custom properties, lifecycle stages, lead status, lists and segments, forms, and workflow automation.
 •    Maintain CRM data quality and governance, including deduplication, field standards, consistent deal stages across pipelines, and clear documentation, so Sales, Customer Growth, and leadership trust the data.
 •    Orchestrate the GTM stack (CRM, app telemtry, data enrichment, and automation tools) so product, marketing, and sales data flow cleanly between systems.
 Enrichment, AI Scoring & Routing 
 •    Build and maintain enrichment workflows that close firmographic, contact, and segment data gaps, including vertical-specific sources relating to childcare, education, and food program participation data.
 •    Design, deploy, and continuously tune fit, intent, and product-usage scoring models, using AI and predictive approaches where they outperform rules-based logic.
 •    Own lead and account routing rules, handoff SLAs, and alerts to Sales and Customer Growth, and monitor speed-to-lead and conversion by route.
 Demand Generation Experiments 
 •    Run a structured demand-gen experimentation program: define the hypothesis, audience, channel, offer, success metric, and decision rule before launch, then scale or move to the next experiment based on results.
 •    Build and execute campaigns, nurture tracks, and outbound sequences against enriched, scored segments, partnering with the Digital Marketing Manager on creative and channel execution.
 •    Use customer, competitive, and market insight to surface new segments and opportunities worth testing, and maintain a prioritized backlog and a visible results log so learnings compound.
 Lifecycle & In-App Engagement 
 •    Own lifecycle programs across the customer journey: onboarding, activation, feature adoption, cross-sell and expansion, renewal, and win-back.
 •    Build behavior-triggered journeys that combine CRM email and telemetry in-app guides, driven by product usage signals rather than calendar cadence alone.
 •    Partner with Product and Customer Growth to identify adoption gaps and cross-sell opportunities across our product portfolio, and run the programs that close them.
 Funnel Reporting & Measurement 
 •    Support maintenance of funnel stage definitions and conversion logic from first touch through closed-won, activation, and expansion.
 •    Build and own dashboards and recurring funnel reporting for RevOps and leadership, covering pipeline, conversion rates, velocity, channel and campaign performance, and product adoption.
 •    Set attribution and experiment measurement standards, and translate the numbers into clear recommendations on where to invest next. We care about great marketing, but ultimately we care about whether it drives growth.
 What Success Looks Like 
 •    First 90 days: You've aligned with product leadership on positioning for priority products; audited HubSpot data, lifecycle stages, and routing; published agreed funnel definitions; shipped a baseline funnel dashboard; and launched your first experiments.
 •    First 6 months: Enrichment and scoring are live and routing leads to Sales and Customer Growth against defined SLAs; core onboarding and adoption journeys are running across email and in-app; and experiments ship on a steady cadence with documented results.
 •    First 12 months: Every feature release runs through a repeatable launch playbook executed in the stack; conversion, speed-to-lead, and product adoption show measurable lift; and leadership uses your funnel reporting to make investment decisions.
 You'll Probably Love This Role If… 
 •    You're a builder who loves making the machine work, not just drawing the diagram. You'd rather ship the test than debate it.
 •    You're curious about customers, competitors, and markets and naturally find yourself asking, “Where's the opportunity here?”
 •    You read a feature release and immediately think about the segment, the trigger, the channel, and the metric.
 •    Messy CRM data bothers you, and you'd rather fix it at the source than patch it in a spreadsheet.
 •    You think in funnels and can explain, in plain language, why a conversion rate moved.
 •    You use AI as a force multiplier in real workflows, from enrichment and scoring to research and content variants, and you know where it helps and where it doesn't.
 •    You’re a natural collaborative and aren’t afraid to step outside of the RevOps team to work with Product, Sales, Customer Growth, and leadership. 
 •    You're comfortable owning your work end to end without needing a huge team around you.
 •    You're excited to build the GTM engine rather than inherit a finished one.
 Required Qualifications 
 •    4+ years in growth marketing, lifecycle marketing, marketing operations, revenue operations, or GTM engineering or a related B2B SaaS role.
 •    Hands-on CRM management/ownership as an admin or power user, including properties, lifecycle stages, workflows, lists, scoring, and reporting.
 •    Experience partnering with product leadership to define positioning and value propositions, and a proven ability to translate individual features into audience-specific messaging deployed across campaigns, lifecycle programs, in-app experiences, and sales enablement.
 •    Experience building data enrichment, lead scoring, and routing, including AI or predictive scoring approaches.
 •    A track record of designing and running demand-gen experiments with clear hypotheses, success metrics, and documented outcomes.
 •    Experience building behavior-triggered lifecycle programs across email and in-app channels.
 •    Strong funnel reporting and analytics skills: defining stages and conversion metrics, building dashboards, and working comfortably with data in spreadsheets or BI tools.
 •    Clear, concise writing, from lifecycle copy to experiment readouts to leadership summaries.
 •    Strong project management and systems thinking, with a habit of documenting what you build.
 •    A builder mentality and the ability to move comfortably between strategy and hands-on execution.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience with CACFP, childcare, child nutrition, education, government programs, or other regulated industries is a huge plus, but not a requirement.
 CACFP has its own language, regulations, acronyms, and complexities. If you already know it, amazing. If you don't, you'll be surrounded by an exceptional team of people who do, and we'll help you get up to speed.
 A few other things we'd love to see:
 •    Experience with vertical SaaS, multi-product portfolios, or marketing to both SMB and enterprise or public-sector buyers.
 •    CRM certifications (Marketing, Sales, or Operations related) or hands-on experience with CRM AI and data enrichment features.
 •    Hands-on experience with in-app engagement or product adoption platforms
 •    Experience with enrichment and GTM automation tools
 •    Technical comfort beyond the UI: SQL, APIs and webhooks, or light scripting (JavaScript or Python) to connect systems and automate workflows.
 •    Comfort building AI-powered workflows for research, enrichment, scoring, and content variation. You know how to make AI your copilot, not your copywriter.
 Why KidKare? 
 We're at an exciting inflection point, taking decades of experience in childcare and child nutrition and using it to build a broader ecosystem of products for the organizations and people who help care for our communities.
 You won't be starting from scratch. We've invested deeply in understanding our customers, markets, competitors, and products. But we're not handing you a finished machine and asking you to keep it running.

Position Title: Medical Secretary Casual 
 Employment Status: Casual (On-Call)
 Position Status: This is a Bargaining Unit position. All terms and conditions of the collective bargaining agreement apply.
This posting is for an existing vacancy.
 Job Posting Deadline for Internal Candidates: July 2, 2026, at 5:00pm
 Hours of Work/Schedule: Casual shifts will be offered as needed for a duration of one Year from Hire. 
 Position Reports To: Manager, Integrated Care and Experience
 Hourly Pay Range: $24.56 - $26. 30 commensurate on skills and experience, plus participation in HOOPP.
 Primary Work Location : Oshawa and Pickering ON; (with flexibility to transition to work at any other DCHC sites as required).
 Organization 
 Durham Community Health Centre (DCHC) is a registered, charitable organization that provides integrated, accessible, and equitable community-based primary care, wellness services, and health education to Durham community members who face multiple barriers to their health and well-being.
 DCHC also provides equity-based programs and services that focus on priority populations such as Indigenous, Black, the 2SLGBTQI Community, Newcomers to Canada, Seniors, and Unattached patients (i.e., those without a family doctor), to name a few. DCHC ensures Durham community members receive not only sick care, but preventive care as well.
 At DCHC, we are a team-based interprofessional group of staff including physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, counselors, dietitians, outreach workers, medical secretaries, and other administrative staff. We always place every client at the centre of our approach to care, based on their needs. We address these needs through integrated clinical and wellness care and health education.
 It's an exciting time to be joining DCHC, while we are embarking on an energizing path with a focus on making our biggest impact yet on local health care by diversifying, expanding, and leveraging our Strategic Plan, Theory of Change, Brand, Client Stories and Resources.
 Position Overview 
 The Medical Secretary will be a welcoming, effective, collaborative member of the Agency’s Clinical Services, Primary Care inter-professional team.  The Medical Secretary works within the Administrative Support Team (AST) to support our primary care service providers.  These include the Registered Nurses, Nurse Practitioners, Physicians and Dietitians on our Medical Services Team (MST) and the Therapists (Registered Social Workers and Registered Psychotherapists) on our Counselling Services Team (CST) as well as the Interprofessional Care Team (IPC). The Medical Secretary will be the first point-of-contact for clients in our community which often includes people who are marginalised and at-risk with respect to the social determinants of health.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Actively contributes to developing and maintaining a welcoming environment for Durham CHC clients and our community by demonstrating a non-judgmental, respectful, and accepting approach to client care – whether meeting clients face-to-face or speaking to clients by telephone.
 Demonstrates excellent customer service skills for our internal and external clients and stakeholders.
 Provides accommodation and maintains accessibility for clients as needed, whenever possible.
 Able to maintain active awareness of people entering and leaving DCHC facilities, ensuring that clients are checked-in, registered for service(s) and ensuring personal awareness of any special requirements/provisions that are noted in the client’s Electronic Health Record (EHR).  Example: When clients are checked-in, ensuring that demographic data, emergency contact information and health card information are maintained and updated.
 Share and/or perform the duties of “Receptionist” when required – and effectively connect clients with the right service at the right place, at the right time.
 Opening and closing DCHC facilities from time-to-time, by following established policy and procedures to ensure client timely access to service and that the building is secured.
 Flexibility to work or drive to meetings at any of DCHC clinical locations in our service area, as required.
 Ability to work a flexible schedule with at least one evening per week.
 Actively maintain awareness and understanding of DCHC services and programs.
 Given that the Medical Secretary will be assigned to specific MST and CST service providers as their “Buddies”, the Medical Secretary will be responsible to collaborate with their Buddies to ensure that their schedules are managed effectively and efficiently (e.g., maintaining full appointment schedules, recalls made in a timely manner etc.) In turn, this will help enable DCHC MST and CST service providers to meet the performance targets that are set by our funders: the Central East Local Health Integration Network (CE-LHIN) and the Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care (MOHLTC) that are described in DCHC Multi-Sector Service Accountability Agreement (MSAA).
 Day-to-day duties of the Medical Secretary include: responding to client and community questions, booking intake and follow-up appointments appropriately, registering new clients, screening and prioritizing of client calls, working with third-parties to arrange and make referrals (e.g., specialist appointments etc.), updating and ensuring that client Electronic Health Record (EHR) is accurate and up-to-date (e.g., scanning, faxing, photocopying, mail distribution and filing are completed in an accurate and timely manner).  Responsibilities also include ensuring specific MST and CST workflow processes are followed and that client forms are updated/maintained and utilised according to policies, procedures and/or practices.  Medical secretary is also responsible for ensuring on-call schedule for providers is maintained.
 Participate in other DCHC staff training activities and team/staff meetings as requested.
 Perform other duties as assigned that are reasonable with the scope of practice for the Medical Secretary.
 Qualifications 
 1.      Completion of a formal 1-year post-Secondary program at a Community College (Office Administration - Health Services).
 2.      Minimum Three (3) Years of recent experience as a Medical Secretary in a Clinical workplace is preferred.  
 3.      More than one year experience working in a medical office triaging calls.
 4.      Access to a car and valid driver’s license required.
 5.      Demonstrated basic understanding of anatomy and physiology, confidentiality and privacy, medical ethics, medical office procedures (including experience in effective use of Electronic Health Record (EHR) , medical terminology and transcription and client/patient management – as core competencies learned in college curriculum.
 6.      Demonstrated ability to support the coordination of collaborative care for clients (i.e., patients) with the Medical Services Team (MST) and Counselling Service Team (CST) service providers.
 7.      Demonstrated competence and experience in helping clients who are experiencing complex physical, mental health/addictions needs.  Demonstrated knowledge of the work of Community Health Centres (CHCs) and the issues affecting marginalized communities and the social determinants of health.  Demonstrates the values of equity, inclusiveness and diversity that are embedded in DCHC Mission, Vision, and Values. 
 8.      Demonstrated knowledge and experience in use of Electronic Health Records (EHR) systems and advanced skills in Microsoft Office (e.g., spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations etc.). Minimum keyboarding speed of 45 net words per minute.
 9.      Excellent oral and written communication skills in English, including active listening and telephone etiquette.
 10.   Demonstrated strong interpersonal, conflict management and crisis intervention skills.  Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training (ASIST) is an asset.
 11.   Excellent attention-to-detail, organizational/planning, time management and problem-solving skills.
 12.   Demonstrated openness to learning and coaching – not afraid to say, “I don’t know, but I will find out.”
 13.   Strong ability to work independently in an inter-professional clinical environment.
 14.   Ability to work effectively and contribute positively in a changing environment.
 Minimum Key Attributes include  Service-oriented, Collaborative, Team Player, Results-oriented, Accountable, Initiative-taking, Flexible, Adaptable, Collaborative, Effective Communication Skills, Ability to manage risk within one’s responsibility and accountability. 
 Role-specific attributes:  Conceptual thinker; Efficient, Organized, Attention to Detail, Creative and Innovative Thinker, Analytical/Systematic, Forward Thinker, Problem-Solving skills, Crisis Management Skills, Empathic.
 Full vaccination against COVID-19 is mandatory for this position (DCHC will however adhere to its duty to accommodate those who are unable to be fully vaccinated for a reason related to a human right protected ground).
 DCHC encourages applications from individuals who reflect the diversity of the communities served, including Indigenous peoples, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community, and other equity-deserving groups. 
 Application Process: 
 1)         While we thank all applicants for their interest in applying, only those qualified and considered for an interview will be contacted. All applicant submissions will be kept on file for six months, for future consideration.
 2)         All applicants are encouraged to provide a valid email address for communication purposes. Applicants may receive written correspondence regarding this job posting directly to the email address provided on their resume. As an applicant, it is your responsibility to ensure that you check your email regularly.
 3)         All positions are subject to the successful completion of the following pre-employment conditions for all external hires: Reference Checks; and Criminal Background checks (including Vulnerable Sector Screening).
 4)         Please be advised that AI Technology supports the screening process of applications. All final hiring decisions are made by our recruitment team.

The Role
 This is a senior client-facing role for someone who wants to operate at the intersection of strategy, growth, sales, and execution.
 You will work directly with founders and business owners, understand their business in depth, identify what is holding growth back, and help them decide what to do next.
 You are not here to simply manage a relationship.
 You are here to become a trusted partner in the growth of the business.
 That means understanding the client's goals, offer, market, acquisition strategy, sales process, delivery model, current constraints, and commercial priorities - then helping them turn that into a clear plan of action.
 In some conversations, you will be helping a founder sharpen their positioning.
 In others, you will be diagnosing why pipeline is weak, why sales are not converting, why execution is stalling, or where the next growth opportunity sits.
 Your job is to create clarity. To tell clients what matters now. To show them what needs to happen next. And to make sure the right actions actually happen.
 This is not a traditional Customer Success role.
 It is a role for someone who wants to become an exceptional commercial operator by working closely with ambitious founders and helping them solve real business problems.
 The Opportunity
 You will have exposure to a large number of businesses, markets, offers, sales models, and growth challenges.
 That creates an unusually steep learning curve.
 Instead of spending years inside one company solving one set of problems, you will see patterns across dozens of businesses and develop the judgment to quickly understand:
 What is actually holding growth back
 What is noise and what matters
 Where the highest-leverage opportunity is
 What the founder should focus on now
 What should be stopped
 What should be doubled down on
 How strategy should translate into execution
 Over time, the expectation is that clients see you as someone whose judgment they trust.
 Someone who can walk into a complicated situation, understand it quickly, simplify it, and give them a clear direction forward.
 If you want to build serious capability in growth strategy, founder communication, sales, operations, and commercial decision-making, this role gives you the environment to do it.
 What You Will Own
 Become a True Growth Partner to Clients
 You will work closely with founders to understand the business beyond surface-level account updates.
 You will build a clear picture of:
 Their business model
 Target market
 ICP
 Offer
 Pricing
 Positioning
 Acquisition channels
 Sales process
 Current pipeline
 Delivery model
 Team capacity
 Growth goals
 Immediate constraints
 From there, you will help determine the highest-priority actions required to move the business forward.
 Advise, Don't Just Support
 We are not looking for someone who simply responds to questions.
 We want someone capable of leading the thinking.
 You should be comfortable saying:
 "This is the problem I think we need to solve first."
 "This is where I think you're focusing on the wrong thing."
 "This is the strategy I would recommend."
 "This is what I would do over the next 30 days."
 "This is what needs to happen before we scale."
 You will challenge clients when needed, simplify decisions, and help them avoid wasting time on low-leverage work.
 Your value comes from your judgment, not just your responsiveness.
 Turn Strategy Into Action
 Good advice without execution is useless.
 Every strategic conversation should translate into clear priorities.
 You will help clients move from broad goals to focused execution:
 Define the objective
 Identify the constraint
 Decide the strategy
 Break it into clear actions
 Assign ownership
 Set timelines
 Review what happened
 Adjust based on results
 You should naturally reduce complexity rather than add to it.
 If a client has fifteen things they could be doing, your job is often to help them identify the two or three that actually matter.
 Help Clients Build Revenue
 You will think commercially.
 That means understanding the complete journey from market to revenue:
 Positioning → Acquisition → Conversations → Pipeline → Sales → Revenue → Delivery → Expansion
 You will help clients understand where that journey is breaking down.
 For example:
 If acquisition is weak, you investigate the offer, market, message, and channel.
 If leads are coming in but deals are not closing, you look at qualification, sales process, follow-up, positioning, and pricing.
 If sales are happening but delivery is becoming difficult, you help identify what needs to change operationally.
 You should be comfortable moving across the business rather than treating growth as a single function.
 Work Across Growth Channels
 Depending on the client, you may be advising across areas such as:
 Cold email
 Outbound
 Paid acquisition
 Offer development
 ICP and positioning
 Lead generation
 CRM and pipeline
 Sales process
 Follow-up
 Proposal strategy
 Pricing
 Go-to-market
 Operational priorities
 AI implementation and services
 You do not need to personally be the world's best practitioner in every function.
 You do need enough commercial understanding to identify what is working, what is not, ask the right questions, and make good strategic recommendations.
 Lead High-Level Client Conversations
 You will spend significant time speaking directly with founders and senior operators.
 These are not scripted check-ins.
 The conversations should be valuable enough that a founder would pay for the thinking itself.
 You will:
 Review business performance
 Analyse what has changed
 Identify opportunities
 Diagnose problems
 Challenge assumptions
 Set priorities
 Recommend strategy
 Help unblock decisions
 Create accountability
 Keep momentum high
 The standard is not whether the meeting happened.
 The standard is whether the meeting changed what happens next.
 Own the Bigger Picture
 Clients may have multiple people supporting different parts of their business.
 Your role is to maintain the full commercial picture.
 You should understand what everyone is working on, how it connects to the overall strategy, and whether the combined effort is actually moving the client toward their objective.
 If teams become disconnected, priorities conflict, or something important is falling through the cracks, you take ownership of resolving it.
 The client should feel like they have one clear strategic partner who understands the whole business.
 Identify Risk Before It Becomes a Problem
 Strong operators notice problems early.
 You should recognise when:
 A client is losing momentum
 Execution has stalled
 The strategy is not producing results
 Expectations have become misaligned
 Lead flow is weak
 Sales follow-up is poor
 Internal delivery is becoming a blocker
 The client is focusing on the wrong priorities
 Trust is beginning to decline
 Then act.
 Do not wait for a formal escalation.
 Part of being a trusted partner is being willing to address uncomfortable realities before they become larger problems.
 Skills & Competencies
 Commercial Judgment
 You understand how businesses grow and make money.
 You can connect strategy to revenue and distinguish between activity and actual commercial progress.
 Strong Diagnostic Ability
 You can listen to a complicated situation and quickly work out what the underlying issue is.
 You separate symptoms from root causes.
 Strategic Thinking
 You can move between the big picture and immediate execution.
 You know how to turn an ambitious goal into the next few actions that actually matter.
 Founder-Level Communication
 You can communicate confidently with intelligent, ambitious, demanding people.
 You are comfortable challenging ideas without becoming confrontational.
 You can give clear advice even when it is not what the client hoped to hear.
 High Ownership
 You do not wait to be told what to do when something is obviously not working.
 You investigate, decide what needs to happen, and move it forward.
 Structured Execution
 You are excellent at turning conversations into decisions, priorities, actions, owners, and timelines.
 Curiosity
 You genuinely enjoy understanding businesses.
 You want to know why an offer works.
 Why one market responds differently from another.
 Why one sales process converts and another does not.
 Why certain founders execute faster than others.
 That curiosity compounds into judgment.
 AI Fluency
 You actively use AI to improve your thinking and output.
 You should use AI to analyse businesses, prepare for conversations, research markets, structure plans, review performance, document decisions, and increase the quality and speed of your work.
 The Person We Want
 This role is best suited to someone who wants to accelerate their career by taking on real responsibility.
 You want to become the kind of person founders trust when making important decisions.
 You want to develop judgment, not just knowledge.
 You want to understand how businesses grow from the inside.
 You are excited by the idea of working across many different companies, seeing patterns quickly, and becoming better at solving commercial problems every week.
 You do not want to spend your career running scripted calls.
 You want to sit across from a founder, understand what they are trying to build, and help them build it.
 You Will Probably Not Fit If
 You want a traditional Customer Success role
 You prefer being given the answer rather than finding it
 You are uncomfortable advising people more senior than you
 You avoid giving direct recommendations
 You prefer following scripts to thinking independently
 You enjoy relationship management but are less interested in business strategy
 You are uncomfortable discussing revenue, sales, pricing, or performance
 You need very clear boundaries around your responsibilities
 You focus heavily on activity rather than outcomes
 You are looking for a low-pressure role with a predictable learning curve
 Experience
 7+ years in consulting, growth, client strategy, account management, sales, operations, or a senior client-facing role
 Experience working directly with founders, executives, or business owners
 Strong commercial understanding and the ability to think across acquisition, sales, and delivery
 Experience helping businesses solve growth or execution problems
 Strong understanding of B2B go-to-market
 Direct exposure to areas such as outbound, sales, offer creation, paid acquisition, pipeline management, consulting, or agency delivery
 Experience operating in fast-moving environments where judgment matters more than rigid process
 What You Get
 Fully remote
 Full-time role at a profitable, bootstrapped company
 Direct access to ambitious founders and business owners
 Exposure to a wide variety of companies, markets, and growth problems
 The opportunity to build deep skill across strategy, acquisition, sales, operations, and AI
 Significant autonomy and ownership
 Direct access to senior leadership
 A role where your judgment and capability can grow quickly
 Performance-based progression into leadership, strategy, operations, or broader commercial ownership
 Independent Contractor Agreement
 This is an opportunity to become much more than an account manager.
 Done well, this role develops you into the kind of commercial operator who can walk into almost any business, understand what matters, and help the founder decide what to do next.

About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





Why we're looking for you



Owner is the leading all-in-one platform for independent restaurants. Operators use Owner to run their online ordering, websites, menus, marketing, and customer experience. Tens of thousands of restaurants depend on us every day to run their business.



Grader is Owner's free restaurant health report. A restaurant owner submits their URL and gets a clear view of where they're losing money online: website performance, Google presence, menu quality, and more. It's one of the most visible products we build and one of the fastest-growing, with significant scale growth ahead and new AI-powered scoring capabilities launching on top of it. The backend powering all of this needs to be fast, resilient, and built to scale.



If you want to own the backend of one of Owner's most strategically important products and set the platform foundation before a major expansion — this is that role.



This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States and Canada.



Our Tech Stack



 - Backend: Node.js, TypeScript

 - Databases: MongoDB, PostgreSQL

 - Infrastructure & Observability: Datadog, AWS, Temporal



The impact you'll have



 - Own the backend services and data pipelines that power Grader scans end-to-end — from ingesting third-party presence signals (Google, Yelp, menus, LLM GEO signals) to serving results reliably at scale

 - Harden the platform before expansion — reduce latency, increase uptime, and build the observability and alerting layer the team needs to confidently scale Grader into new scoring dimensions

 - Establish platform foundations — shared abstractions, operational runbooks, and architectural patterns that reduce toil and give other engineers a reliable base to build on

 - Partner closely with PLG product and the AI Agents team as Grader evolves into a broader AI-powered tool for restaurant owners



What we're looking for

 - Experience building and operating data pipelines, third-party integrations, and async processing systems at scale

 - Proven track record improving system reliability — observability, alerting, incident reduction, and making operational health a team habit

 - Experience at a product-focused startup or scale-up where you owned systems end-to-end

 - High degree of cross-functional collaboration — past colleagues in product, design, and business would speak highly of your teamwork

 - Strong sense of ownership and drive, excellent communication, and a proactive approach to identifying and solving problems

 We're a small, elite team of AI researchers and engineers building predictive models across commodities, prediction markets, and global macro. We're well capitalized, we move fast, and we care about one thing above all: whether a signal actually works.
 The Alpha Signal Program is how we bring in talent from outside the usual channels. We've found that the people with real edge aren't always the ones with the right CV or the right address.
 The opportunity
 This isn't a conventional job, and we'd rather be upfront about that. You won't be assigned a desk or a manager. Instead, you bring us a signal — a model, a systematic strategy, a way of reading a market that you believe gives you an edge — and we put real capital behind it. We handle the execution, the risk, and the infrastructure. You're paid a performance fee tied directly to how your signal performs.
 You can do this from anywhere in the world, on your own schedule, alongside whatever else you're doing. If your signal works, the upside is yours to share in. If it doesn't, you've lost nothing but the time it took to find out.
 What you'd be working on
 You'd develop and refine predictive signals in one or more of the following areas:
 Commodities — energy, metals, agriculture, and the relationships between them, physical and financial.
 Prediction markets — event probabilities and mispriced odds, wherever information becomes a price.
 Global macro — rates, FX, sovereign risk, and cross-asset calls, systematic.
 We don't filter on pedigree. You might be a quant, a full-time trader, an academic, or entirely self-taught. What matters is that you can show us a genuine edge and explain why it holds up.
 We're especially keen to hear from:
 Self-directed traders with a verifiable track record but no institutional name behind them
 Researchers from physics, mathematics, engineering, or computer science who apply their tools to markets
 Specialists who understand one corner of the world — a commodity, an energy market, an election — better than the Street does
 Anyone who has been right often enough to know it isn't luck
 A performance fee tied directly to what your signal earns — the stronger and more consistent it is, the larger your share
 Real capital behind your ideas, plus institutional-grade execution and risk management
 Complete flexibility: fully remote, work from anywhere, on your own time
 No relocation, no employment requirement to begin, and no obligation to share anything sensitive before an NDA is in place
 The chance to work alongside a world-class team of AI researchers and engineers who will push your thinking harder than anyone else
 How to apply
 Click apply and attach your supporting material — your CV, a track record, a short description of your signal or approach, or whatever best makes your case. You don't need to give away how your edge works at this stage; we just want a clear picture of who you are and what you bring.

 Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.
 Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.
 Un employeur de choix 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.
 Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe? 
 Nous recherchons un gestionnaire de projets techniques pour rejoindre notre équipe de la chaîne d'approvisionnement.  Leadership de projet: Planifier, exécuter et surveiller les projets techniques, de transition et de ressources conformément aux processus et normes de l'entreprise.
 Coordination interfonctionnelle: Dirigez et alignez des équipes multidisciplinaires — incluant l'ingénierie, la qualité, les achats, le laboratoire et l'inspection — afin de mener les projets techniques à la clôture.
 Collaboration avec les fournisseurs: Effectuer des examens formels de projet avec les fournisseurs et collaborer avec des spécialistes des comptes internes pour maintenir l'alignement sur la portée du projet et les livrables.
 Amélioration des processus: Identifiez, dirigez et soutenez des initiatives visant à résoudre les problèmes de productibilité, à réduire les coûts et à rationaliser les flux de travail opérationnels.
 Suivi et administration: Maintenir des échéanciers réalistes mais ambitieux des projets, gérer les transactions SAP liées aux projets et suivre les indicateurs de réduction des coûts.
 Ce que vous apprendrez 
 Maîtrise technique de la chaîne d'approvisionnement: approfondissez votre expertise dans les opérations interfonctionnelles de la chaîne d'approvisionnement dans un environnement d'ingénierie complexe.
 Leadership des fournisseurs: Affinez vos compétences en négociation et gestion grâce à un engagement direct et des revues stratégiques avec des fournisseurs externes.
 Expertise en ERP d'entreprise: Développez des compétences avancées en suivi de projets et gestion des transactions au sein de SAP.
 Qu’est-ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir? 
 Formation et expérience: Baccalauréat dans un domaine pertinent (par exemple, génie, affaires, chaîne d'approvisionnement) ou expérience pratique équivalente, plus 3+ ans d'expérience en gestion technique de projet.
 Compétences linguistiques: Maîtrise professionnelle du français et de l'anglais (oral et écrit).
 Compétences techniques: Maîtrise de la suite Microsoft Office.
 Compétences clés: Capacité de leadership éprouvée, solides aptitudes organisationnelles, automotivation et un état d'esprit d'amélioration continue.
 Ce poste s’inscrit dans un milieu de travail francophone, néanmoins il nécessite une très bonne connaissance de l’anglais pour lire et comprendre, sur une base quotidienne, de la documentation et des termes techniques qui peuvent émaner d’organisations internationales, ainsi que pour écrire et communiquer en anglais avec des clients, des fournisseurs ou des collègues internationaux.

 Programme de santé et bien-être, y compris la télémédecine

We're transforming the grocery industry 
 At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. 
 Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.
 Instacart is a Flex First team 
 There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work. 
 OVERVIEW
 Every year, people across the world spend nearly one trillion dollars on groceries. It’s an industry that’s been around for centuries. Food itself, however, has been a constant in people’s lives since the beginning of time. Yes, sustenance is essential, but it’s also much more than that. Food can be a part of a daily ritual or a special moment that resonates with people on a meaningful and emotional level. It can be a much-needed break in a long day, a taste that brings back memories, a creative experiment, a shared meal with loved ones, or even comfort during a hard time. Whether it’s a special occasion or an everyday occurrence, it should always be easy for people to get the ingredients they need.
 The Instacart Design Team is dedicated to making grocery shopping effortless for everyone and finding solutions to large-scale opportunities that will forever change the way people feed themselves and their loved ones. We’re a four sided marketplace and design for the needs of Consumer, Shoppers, Retailers, and Advertisers.
 Within the Instacart Design org, we have exciting roles that will drive meaningful business impact through thoughtful strategy, experimentation, and high-quality execution. We design the end-to-end journeys that help customers discover, understand, and feel the undeniable value of Instacart, putting empathy for both prospective and existing members at the center of every decision. Our team blends product thinking, brand-forward storytelling, and behavioral insight to create cohesive, high-performing growth experiences. We pride ourselves on a culture of experimentation, accountability, and craft, continuously evolving how we design for conversion, retention, and long-term customer value.
 We’re hiring for a Staff Experience Designer to join the Core Experience team and lead work across multiple touchpoints along our end to end online grocery experience in app. You’ll obsess user, cultural and industry shifts in food and shopping spaces and inspire new features that come with strong value propositions that can be uniquely owned by the Intacart brand experience and online grocery ecosystem. This role will need to work very closely with teams across the end to end shopping experience as well as new modalities that help deliver experiences through AI and agentic based conversational interfaces. This is a high-impact, highly collaborative role partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Brand, Data Science, and Research to drive measurable business outcomes while strengthening customer trust, affinity for the brand and long-term loyalty. 
 About The Job
 Daily Rhythms and Samples of Work
 Drive and lead experiences across consumer-facing products to create highly personalized journeys that meet households where they are — their routines, their needs, their goals — and build new layers of value into the core grocery experience.
 Lead end-to-end experience design briefs across all surfaces and modalities, including agentic interfaces, that deepen how customers discover, shop, and build lasting habits with Instacart.
 Craft narratives, naming, and value propositions for experiences and features, creating artifacts (strategy docs, flows, storyboards, internal decks) that help teams socialize strategies and ideas.
 Define and own experience frameworks that map key journeys (first 3 orders, building repeat patterns, subscription adoption, household management) and clearly articulate the beats, rhythms, and jobs to be done at each step.
 Shape content, hierarchy, and information architecture across surfaces: define how information is structured, named, and prioritized so users have clear comprehension at every step while the business and partners get the right visibility where it matters.
 Codify experiential principles, functional and emotional, to guide what users should understand, decide, and feel across flows, then translate those principles into patterns, content hierarchies, and interaction rules that scale across teams.
 Use AI-assisted prototyping and concept development as a core part of your practice, providing strong art direction, references, and experiential intent to generate flows and concepts that align with Instacart's design system, brand positioning, and evolving interaction patterns.
 Design for visual clarity, pacing, and density, establishing patterns, grids, and rules that govern how modules, carousels, and key placements work (above vs. below the fold) to balance user needs, business objectives, and partner value.
 Work with Research, and sometimes lead or plan it yourself, to uncover insights about how customers shop, build routines, and evolve over their lifecycle with Instacart, then translate those insights into concrete journey maps, flows, and experiential principles.
 Raise the bar for experience-led thinking across the pods, mentoring partners on how to think in journeys and emotions rather than just screens, and advocating for cohesive, principle-driven experiences that feel uniquely Instacart.

 The Woodfibre LNG Project is located approximately 7 km west-southwest of Squamish, British Columbia. It involves the construction and operation of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) export facility on the previous Woodfibre pulp mill site, which would have a storage capacity of 250,000 m3 and would produce approximately 2.1 million tons per year of LNG.
 Woodfibre Management Ltd. is a privately held Canadian company based in Vancouver and a subsidiary of Pacific Energy Corporation Limited.
 Job Summary 
 Woodfibre LNG is looking for an experienced Electrical Technicians to join our dynamic team. Reporting directly to the Electrical & Instrumentation Supervisor , the successful candidate will be responsible for installing, maintaining, troubleshooting, and repairing electrical systems at our facility. This role offers the opportunity to be part of a dedicated team that ensures the safe, reliable, efficient, and environmentally responsible operation of the Woodfibre LNG Plant. 
 Key Responsibilities : 
 Support the commissioning and start-up of the LNG plant at both the Squamish site as well as our yard in China if required
 Perform scheduled preventative, predictive, routine, turnaround and emergency maintenance of industrial electrical equipment, including motors, starters, VFDs, UPS systems, EHT, relays, breakers, switchgear, etc.
 Troubleshoot electrical systems, including 120V-4160V circuits, control systems, HVAC, cathodic protection, and electrical heat trace.
 Inspect electrical systems and components to identify hazards, defects, and perform necessary repairs.
 Transformer monitoring and maintenance on dry and oil bath types
 Interpret drawings, apply the Canadian Electrical Code (CEC), and follow installation standards.
 Experience working with 600V, 4160V systems.  HV experience considered an asset

 Ensure compliance with safety procedures, including Arc Flash and Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO).
 Knowledgeable of DCS systems, PLC’s, and HMI’s
 Respond to after-hour callouts and maintain a safe, organized work environment.
 Support the site’s maintenance program, including keeping up-to-date records of all maintenance, repairs, and calibrations performed via our CMMS.
 Review process flow drawings, equipment lists, and specifications to resolve work procedures.
 Collaborate with internal teams and third-party service providers.
 Contribute to the continuous improvement of maintenance key performance indicators.
 HSSE 
 100% compliance with company HSE policies and guidelines.
 Champion HSE as a member of the LNG Operations Team.
 Lead HSE Shift Meeting/ safety walks/audits if and when required.
 Timely intervention to mitigate risks and ensure the safety of personnel and plant.
 Demonstrate a personal commitment to influence overall safety behavior in the plant.
 Safeguarding systems check lists are implemented/completed by Shift Operations to agreed frequencies and standards.
 Execute plant wide operations hazards awareness program. 
 Initiate inputs for plant risk register and mitigation tracking process for operations.
 Required Experience 
 Minimum 5+ years of relevant industrial maintenance experience 
 Valid British Columbia Journeyman ticket or Red Seal certification 
 Dual Electrical & Instrumentation ticket considered an asset
 Experience with Medium Voltage VFD’s considered an asset
 Previous Commissioning and Start-up experience an asset

 Your role will go beyond analysis and recommendations. You will lead the execution of a defined transformation mandate, coordinating teams, supporting adoption, and delivering measurable results. Your work will contribute to the decisions that shape the business day to day, from improving processes and systems to customer experience, talent development, and financial performance. 
 At Valsoft, an entrepreneurial mindset is fundamental to success. We expect our leaders to think and act like owners: identify opportunities, make informed decisions quickly, take calculated risks, and remain accountable for results. This is a role for someone energized by building and improving a business. 
 Managing Director Track  
 The Managing Director Track is designed for ambitious early career leaders who have the potential and ambition to lead a company. Candidates who demonstrate ability to deliver sustained business results, sound judgment, strong leadership capability, and alignment with our values may be considered for a Managing Director role within 12 to 24 months, subject to readiness and the availability of an appropriate opportunity. 
 Your role  
 Own the transformation plan, key performance indicators, and improvement priorities for a defined mandate or operating area. 
 Identify and prioritize opportunities to improve revenue, pricing, customer retention, cost performance, service delivery, processes, and systems. 
 Build a strong understanding of the business, its customers, its financial performance, and its competitive environment. 
 Translate strategic priorities into clear actions, accountabilities, and measurable outcomes. 
 Lead priority transformation initiatives from diagnosis through implementation, coordinating stakeholders, supporting adoption, and measuring operating and financial impact. 
 Partner with the Managing Director and senior leadership team on business planning, performance reviews, and major decisions. 
 Engage and support teams affected by change while building a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement. 
 Collaborate with leaders across the portfolio to share best practices and support business improvement initiatives. 
 Your growth  
 Building a stronger business requires curiosity, resilience, sound judgment, and a willingness to take responsibility when the path forward is not obvious. You will receive practical experience, clear feedback, and direct support as you build your leadership capability. 
 Direct exposure to senior leadership: Work closely with experienced operators and business leaders who will invest in your development and hold you to a high standard 
 A senior mentor: Receive coaching and feedback from a designated mentor as you build the judgment required to lead a business 
 Learning through ownership: Develop by taking responsibility for real business outcomes, not by observing from the sidelines 
 A network across the group: Learn from leaders in other portfolio companies and gain exposure to different businesses and operating environments 
 Your qualifications and skills

 4 to 7 years of professional experience

 Excellent communication skills and the ability to build trust across teams and levels of an organization

 A strong ownership mindset, commercial curiosity, and genuine ambition to build and lead a business

 Compensation and benefits  
 Competitive base salary and performance based incentive. 
 Comprehensive health benefits. 
 Unlimited vacation.
